items.text: – No peeking. If you peek, I'll sew you up.
items.q: Niloofar playfully threatens Amir if he opens his eyes. Is 'I'll sew you up' clear as a joking threat?
before: It occurred to me that if no one had ever been there, his feet could not reach it either, and his presence would no longer bother me. Only me and Niloofar. Niloofar closed her eyes, and I closed mine too.

items.text: He says, "A good year is known from its spring."
items.q: Maman quotes a Persian saying, kept close to literal, that Ghassem uses as a joke. Can you guess its meaning?

items.text: – I thought, now that you've come from abroad, let me serve you the guts of friendship on a tray.
items.q: Hooman treats a friend to tea. 'serve you the guts of friendship on a tray' is a kept Persian image. Can you guess its meaning?
before: – You never used to do things like this?

items.text: – No problem. I'll fight both of you at once, since you guys are both like little finches to me.
items.q: A big teenager scoffs at two small boys who want to fight him. Is 'like little finches to me' clear?
before: Negar's cousin glanced at me and said:

items.text: – But I say, I wish at least things had worked out for you with Her Ladyship Ms. Armaaan ...
items.q: Hooman mockingly stretches the girl's surname, Arman. Does 'Her Ladyship Ms. Armaaan' come across as teasing?
before: – Eldie, see how far you've taken it: Farid, who doesn't give a damn about us or the room or anyone, has spoken up.

items.text: – You lot go stick to your jigily-jigily pop and Soosan Khanom. What business do you have listening to Moein?
items.q: Eskandar sneers at his roommates' taste in cheap pop music. Does 'jigily-jigily pop' work for that?

items.text: – He had become so thin and dark, that brainless ape.
items.q: Maman, mocking a man she dislikes, calls him this. Does 'that brainless ape' sound natural from a mother?
before: We laugh. Maman, her head now between Omid's head and the Boteh-Jegheh patterns on the pillow beneath her head, says:

items.text: – The one with the silly teacher? Mm-hm, watch that one. It's funny. Laugh a little.
items.q: Maman encourages her family to watch a comedy. Does it sound like her?

items.text: When he came back from Karbala, he'd put on a white glove. We walked all the way from the boulevard home, and he kept lifting his hand, as if his hand were something holy for people to kiss.
items.q: Maman mocks her husband's airs after a pilgrimage. Does this sound like her?

items.text: – Amir, is having the lead role a good thing?
items.q: Maman has heard she has the lead role in a book. Does her question sound innocent and natural?
before: – Oh, when he said there are six hundred and some characters in his book, Maman asked him: am I in the book too? Hashem said, you have the lead role.

items.text: – He'd been drinking too much soda.
items.q: Maman explains what she thinks caused the young man's death. Does her line sound natural?

items.text: – At the hospital they kept calling out, "Family of Mrs. Adham!" Nobody moved. Then the nurse herself came over and said, "I think she's yours."
items.q: Maman tells how the hospital called for Naney's family by her surname. Does it sound like her?

items.text: – Ugh, every time you ask him to get something, it's like he gets an electric shock.
items.q: Maman complains about a son who hates errands. Does this sound natural?

items.text: – He complains for no reason, heh, Amir-jan. If it isn't this, he'll find something else.
items.q: Maman waves off a complaint. Does 'heh' sound natural in her speech?

items.text: – Is this how you say thank you?
items.q: Maman scolds through clenched teeth. Does this sound natural?

items.text: – Where did such a wave come from?
items.q: Maman sees a tsunami on television. Does her question sound natural?
before: – Amir, come look what a wave it's making.
